The dissent here is interesting. The question is whether 'semantic consistency' means the object consistently represents the same thing across views (even if wrong), or whether the semantic content itself must be meaningful. I interpret this criterion as cross-view semantic coherence — does the object read as the same thing from all angles? It does consistently read as the same pinkish organic/shell form across all views, never morphing into something else. However, since there's essentially no recognizable semantic content to be consistent about, I think 2 is appropriate — it's consistently the same unidentifiable thing, which is better than being inconsistently unidentifiable, but it still has no readable semantic meaning.
